analysis:
The change is documentation only, in docs/developer/build.md. It adds (a) a CMake install note (head lines 170-174), (b) CI routing behavior for push runs (head lines 273-277), and (c) a new CI Caching section (head lines 300-384). No provider runtime code, protocol, attestation, key handling or coordinator contract is modified. I found no direct effect on TB-002, TB-011, A-003, A-015 or A-016.

Security-relevant claims examined:
- Cache saves only on push to master/dev, with PR caches scoped to the merge ref. This is a sound cache-poisoning posture: untrusted PR code cannot seed caches that master or release builds restore. The docs state PR caches do not seed master. That is only documentation; the enforcing workflow (ci.yml SAVE_CACHES, provider-ci-build action) is not supplied here, so the claim is unverified.
- The CMake note says release tooling reuses a runner-provided CMake 3.31.12 at $RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE if a universal.complete marker exists and the binary reports that exact version. Otherwise it downloads and verifies the archive. This version check does not verify a checksum of the pre-unpacked binary. Release builds use literal Blacksmith labels per the doc, so Darkbloom sandbox images should not reach signing lanes. The behavior of scripts/install-release-cmake.sh is not visible. This is a possible supply-chain question for the next reviewer, not an established regression.
- Push runs now request Darkbloom sandbox routing. The plane's approval decides which branches are admitted, and the request names only repo, run and lanes. Routed jobs are read-only and release, signing and publication jobs keep literal Blacksmith labels, which are outside this change. The workflow and script changes are outside the supplied evidence.
- The sparse checkout (blob:none, skipping evidence tarballs) and the .git cache with an fsck gate and persist-credentials: false are consistent with not persisting tokens in caches.

The patch excerpt is truncated and the workflow, action and script files are not in this batch, so the actual enforcement of these documented controls is unverified.
